basis: Thymic tumour; supplied classification places thymus among endocrine glands. An epithelial thymic tumour does not itself establish lymphoma or immunodeficiency.
Defined by progressive neurodegeneration and blindness; severe developmental impairment, seizures, spasticity and blindness occur in 80–99%.
Radiation-induced spinal cord white matter injury defines this disease; no additional organ involvement established.
Encephalopathy and hearing loss define it; scoliosis 3/3 and optic atrophy 1/3 support involvement. Neurogenic bladder 1/3 omitted by cap; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Congenital neutrophil deficiency is a blood-cell disorder and innate immunodeficiency; recurrent infections do not establish common damage to another organ.
Gastrinoma-driven hypergastrinemia and acid-mediated peptic ulceration/esophagitis define the syndrome; other endocrine tumours are minority MEN1-associated findings.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy; hearing loss 80–99%. Optic atrophy and multiple lipomas each 30–79% are omitted by the four-axis cap.
Acute myeloid leukemia affects marrow and myeloid blood cells. Other KIT-associated tumour types in the definition are separate diseases.
Sensorimotor neuropathy; muscle atrophy and pes cavus 80–99%, contractures 30–79%; persistent vocal cord paresis affects the larynx in 30–79%.
Plasmalogen biosynthesis disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment/spasticity and cataracts are common (>30%) across the major FAR1 deficiency and upregulation phenotypes.
Developmental and intellectual impairment are common across partial chromosome 20 duplication syndromes; other organ malformations vary with the duplicated segment.
ANGPTL3-related low LDL and triglycerides define a lipid metabolism disorder; common direct hepatic or neurologic injury is not established.
Corneal protein deposition causes vision impairment and recurrent corneal erosions; disease is confined to the ocular axis.
Inherited biochemical pathway defects define this broad metabolic umbrella; no additional organ is consistently damaged across most constituent diseases.
Immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease; psoriatic arthritis is a separately diagnosed disease, and cardiovascular disease is an associated risk.
HSV-2 infection typically produces genital cutaneous vesicles and ulcers; neurologic complications are a minority and do not qualify.
Developmental/intellectual impairment is the core supported manifestation; variable cardiac and other congenital anomalies lack evidence of common involvement here.
Developmental/intellectual impairment commonly accompanies 12q deletions; skeletal and visceral malformations depend on the deleted interval and are not uniform across this umbrella.
HDV directly infects and inflames the liver; cirrhosis remains hepatic. Confusion and bleeding are occasional and do not establish another organ axis.
Profound neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; cataracts occur in 5/5 and hearing impairment in 2/5. Precocious puberty occurs in only 1/5.
Defined retinal degeneration with rod-cone dystrophy in 3/3; explicitly classified as a congenital glycosylation disorder. Unquantified systemic features do not establish involvement.
Benign neoplasm arising in skin epithelium; infectious causation in wart subtypes does not apply across this tumour umbrella.
Usher type 1B is defined by retinal degeneration, congenital sensorineural deafness and vestibular dysfunction; vestibular dysfunction belongs to the otologic axis.
Mitochondrial optic atrophy; hearing loss and myopathy each 30–79%. Neuropathy and ataxia are occasional (5–29%); diabetes and cardiomyopathy are very rare.
Congenital malformations of capillary vessels, predominantly presenting as cutaneous vascular lesions; systemic organ injury is subtype-dependent.
